Subject: Quantix Health — tenancy recommendation & burst-lane proposal

Liam / Quantix team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great conversation and appreciate the clarity around PHI flows and the pilot scope. High-level ask from your side: a recommendation and cost/operational plan that shows (a) a Private deployment footprint that meets your compliance needs (air-gapped option), and (b) a Dedicated (reserved) capacity path if you prefer managed GPU pools — with a clear burst/fallback lane so we can scale for spikes during clinical ingestion windows.

Key constraints you reiterated:
- All PHI must remain within isolated tenant environment (no cross-tenant KV caching).
- Pilot expected to start mid-Q4 (3 month pilot) with steady-state ~120 req/s and peak bursts up to ~1.2k req/s for short windows (10–15 mins).
- Typical prompt/response token mix ~1k tokens average, seq len ~512 for longer LLM ops.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 300ms for interactive endpoints; background batch can be higher.

Can you put together a recommendation that covers:
1) GPU-sizing (types + counts) for both Dedicated and Private footprints,
2) a viable hybrid/burst model (how we safely burst to hosted or dedicated spare pool while preserving PHI controls),
3) rough cost delta (monthly) and the procurement/contract ask (commit size / term), and
4) a short mutual action plan for the next 6 weeks so Quantix can share with their procurement/legal folks.

I've attached your usage projection sheet you shared and a blank MAP template. Please flag any assumptions.

Thanks — Evelyn

--

Subject: Re: Quantix Health — tenancy recommendation & burst-lane proposal

Evelyn / team / Liam,

Thanks — ran through the projection sheet and sketched two feasible configurations. Quick summary up front: my recommendation is a Dedicated-first baseline with a controlled burst lane into a private-hosted burst pool (non-PHI) or into an isolated reserved burst pool that we keep for regulated spikes. Private (air-gapped on-prem) is feasible but increases capex and on-call surface — I'll highlight tradeoffs below.

Option A — Dedicated (managed GPU pool) + isolated tenant: recommended baseline
- Baseline: 4 x NVIDIA A100-80GB (dedicated GPU nodes) in a single-region reserved pool.
  - Rationale: per-token performance + memory for KV caching at 1k token responses, good for batching and long context.
  - Expected steady throughput: ~120 req/s with 95th latencies around 180–250ms with continuous batching (batch target ~64 tokens per forward).
- Burst lane: pre-warmed spare capacity of 8 x A10 GPUs (cheaper, lower latency for short-response tasks) that can be routed during 10–15 min spikes via policy.
- Autoscaling: conservative policy — keep baseline cold-start <30s; burst uses warm pool to maintain latency.
- Security: tenant isolation, no cross-tenant KV cache; network egress restricted to Quantix VPC peering.
- Cost: approx $95k/month (baseline + burst reserve amortized) — see attached costing sheet.

Option B — Private (customer VPC or on-prem) — higher isolation, higher ops
- Private control plane with customer-managed compute. Suggested config for pilot: 6 x H100 80GB (on-prem or in-customer-dedicated-hosts).
  - Rationale: provides headroom for larger model variants, highest throughput.
  - Steady throughput: easily covers 120 req/s with 95th ~140–200ms depending on SW stack.
  - Bursting: limited — would need either a dedicated cold standby or a contractual burst to Redwood Dedicated (requires secure egress rules and BAA-level agreement).
- Tradeoffs: ~1.6x higher monthly TCO when you include ops/support and longer procurement lead times (hardware delivery).

Hybrid recommendation (short):
- Pilot: start Dedicated baseline (Option A) with SLA and reserved commit for 3–6 months to prove integrations.
- If Quantix requires air-gap for PHI, run inference in Private but keep lightweight orchestration in private control plane and use Dedicated as a burst option for non-PHI workloads.

Sizing assumptions and notes:
- Avg tokens: 1k output+input => model selection matters (we recommend an 1.4B/2.7B family quantized Q4 profile for cost vs quality tradeoff).
- KV caching: disabled for PHI-sensitive payloads unless explicit tokenization and retention policies are accepted — we've assumed no persistent KV for PHI.
- Failover: set route-level fallbacks to a smaller model family with strict redaction for extreme capacity events.

I've attached a quick costing export and a model/throughput worksheet. Happy to walk through on a call; can prepare a slide that maps config->procurement ask.

Regards,
Aditya

Evelyn / team / Liam,

A few procurement and contract notes from my side:
- If Quantix is comfortable with Dedicated baseline, offer a 12-month reserved commit with quarterly consumption reconciliation. That gets you ~18% discount vs month-to-month and guarantees burst lane capacity at pre-negotiated rates.
- For Private deployments (air-gapped), Legal will require the standard platform license + installation fee. Lead time for on-prem hardware ordering (H100s) is ~8–12 weeks.
- For the MAP: include an explicit acceptance criteria item for latency SLOs, PHI handling responsibilities, and a clause about fallback to a smaller model family with pre-approved redaction logic.

Procurement contact (to engage): procurement@quantixhealth.com — please ask them to share vendor onboarding requirements.

Quick note to Liam: we can draft a short statement of work (SOW) that lists the baseline capacity, burst mechanics, and rollback rules. If you want, we can fold in a short ramp schedule tied to pilot milestones.

—Priyom
